Create a Shape

Source: R/array.R
shp.Rd

Creates the shape of an array from its axis sizes: shp(2, 3) is the shape of a 2x3 matrix, and shp() is the shape of a scalar, which has no axes.

The result is the integer vector that shape() returns, so it can be passed to any shape argument and compared with identical(shape(x), shp(2, 3)). Unlike c(), which returns NULL when called without arguments, shp() always returns an integer vector. A shape argument refuses NULL, so a NULL that slips in by accident – such as the dim() of a vector – is an error rather than the shape of a scalar.

Usage

shp(...)

Arguments

...

(numeric())
The axis sizes: non-negative whole numbers. Vectors are spliced in, so shp(shape(x), 3) appends an axis of size 3 to the shape of x. NULL, a logical and a factor are refused.

Value

(integer())
The axis sizes.

See also

shape() for the shape of an array, nv_array().

Examples

shp(2, 3)
#> [1] 2 3
# the shape of a scalar
shp()
#> integer(0)
# vectors are spliced in
shp(c(2, 3), 4)
#> [1] 2 3 4
nv_array(1:6, shape = shp(2, 3))
#> AnvlArray
#>  1 3 5
#>  2 4 6
#> [ CPUi32{2,3} ] 
nv_array(1L, shape = shp())
#> AnvlArray
#>  1
#> [ CPUi32{} ]
